distinguishing_features: Replaces continuous tubes with segmented tubes connected by geometrically integrated flexible hinges
Alters the tube's own structural geometry to decouple vibrational modes along the length
Uses localized cross-section changes (necks/collars) as mechanical hinges without external supports
Shifts local natural frequencies by shortening effective span length via segmentation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to suppress flow-induced vibration fatigue in shell-and-tube heat exchanger tubes without relying on external support modifications or active monitoring, by fundamentally altering the tube's dynamic response to avoid resonance with vortex shedding frequencies
parsed.viable_reason: The segmented tube with integrated hinges introduces unproven mechanical complexity in a high-pressure, high-temperature environment where leak-tightness and structural integrity are critical, and the hinges would likely create unacceptable stress concentrations or leakage paths as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The concept of using intrinsic geometric segmentation to decouple vibrational modes represents a fundamental departure from both standard design practices and prior-art monitoring approaches, and would not be an obvious adaptation of signal-based vibration inference methods.
